title: Vehicle-Program Allowance in Good-Faith Days for Kestrel Auto Finance Borrowers
content:
A deferral qualifying payment on Kestrel Auto Finance Retail Installment Contracts also carries a good-faith amount, applied to principal, equal to one day's interest on the principal balance at the contract APR over the tier's day-count basis multiplied by the good-faith days and rounded to the cent.

The good-faith days are raised by a vehicle-program allowance read from the purchase order the contract finances — the vehicle program under which the vehicle was sold, as recorded on the customer's Vehicle Purchase Agreements order.

| Vehicle program on the financed purchase order | Days added |
|---|---|
| Kestrel Value Line | entry-program good-faith days: 5 |
| Kestrel Inspected | entry-program good-faith days: 5 |
| Kestrel Certified | certified-program good-faith days: 2 |
| Kestrel Certified Plus | certified-program good-faith days: 2 |
| any higher program | none |

## Reading the schedule

- The program is read from the financed purchase order, not from the borrower's description of the vehicle.
- Hypothetical: good-faith days of 15 on a vehicle sold under Kestrel Inspected become 20; on a vehicle sold under Kestrel Certified Plus they become 17.
- Hypothetical: a borrower whose good-faith days would otherwise be none, on a vehicle sold under Kestrel Value Line, has 5 days; on a principal balance of 9800.00 at 15.59 percent over a 365-day basis that is a good-faith amount of 20.93.
